transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-10
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Acme CTO), Aisha Khan (Eng Mgr), Sam O'Neill (SRE), Lina Gomez (Head of Security)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/deck/console-tracing (deck), https://redwood.ai/samples/trace-queries (playbook), shared spreadsheet: acme-benchmarks.xlsx (not attached)

Summary:
High-level console walkthrough focusing on tracing, error analysis, request logs, and debugging flows. Customer interested in how Redwood surfaces request-level traces, correlates errors to model versions, and supports private deployments (VPC, KMS). Agreed next steps: send pricing/TCO, share recording and queries, customer to provide sample logs for a POC benchmark.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jamie, AE at Redwood, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, Priya here. we'll jump into the console and do some tracing + request logs debugging, show how errors surface and how you can query by model/version, route, and KV cache hit rate.
[00:18] Marcus (Acme CTO): Cool. quick context, we have a prod-ish environment on GCP, about 200k tokens/day, and we're evaluating whether dedicated capacity or private deployment is necessary for data residency and latency.
[00:29] Aisha (Eng Mgr): Yeah and we care about noisy failures — sometimes requests time out or return hallucinations, want to see root cause and correlate to rollout.
[00:39] Priya: absolutely, we'll demo a typical debugging flow: start from the error in Sentry-like alert, jump into a trace, inspect span timeline, request payload, model variant and kv cache hit/miss, and then look at request logs to see upstream latencies.
[00:53] Sam (SRE): quick Q — can we ingest our existing logs into Redwood console or do we rely only on Redwood request logs?
[01:02] Priya: short answer: you can push logs via our API or integrate with Cloud Logging — we also ingest request logs from the serving runtime. so you can correlate. there's a small mapping step for trace ids.
[01:14] Lina (Security): Does request logs contain PII? How is data encrypted at rest — KMS?
[01:20] Jamie: yes, data at rest is encrypted with KMS and we support customer-managed keys for private deployments. we also have retention controls and can redact fields at ingestion if needed. we'll send the security pack after this call.
[01:33] Marcus: great. let's see the console.
[01:36] Priya: ok share screen — starting at the console home, nav to Observability -> Traces. you'll see a heatmap of latency and error rates by route and model.
[01:46] [01:46] Priya: (screen) so here's a spike in errors for the /generate-chat route around 10:23 UTC. clicking into that brings up the trace view.
[01:53] [02:03] Priya: trace view shows span breakdown — client -> router -> model-house (or model-pool), with per-span timing. notice the KV cache span — you'll see hit vs miss percentage. if many misses you'll see higher model compute time.
[02:18] Aisha: sometimes we see large variance in latency; is that KV cache related or batching?
[02:24] Priya: could be both. we show per-request batch size and whether request was served from prefix cache. batching is visible in the spans; we also show kernel choice and quantization hint (sometimes fuzzy in the transcription, kernel -> carnel).
[02:38] Sam: can we filter traces by model version and by routing policy (latency-first vs cost-first)?
[02:44] Priya: yes, we have filters top-right — model.version, route, region, and routing policy. you can save a filter and set alerts on it.
[02:52] [03:08] Priya: now drill into a failing request — here's the request payload; pro tip: we surface the prompt tokens, truncated context and the full response. sometimes ASR of names is off in transcript exports; but the data is verbatim.
[03:22] Marcus: can we see which model variant was used when the hallucination occurred? that was a concern for product folks.
[03:28] Priya: yes the trace includes model.catalog entry and model.hash. we also show if a fallback happened — e.g., main model failed and routed to a smaller compat variant; that's annotated in the trace with a fallback span.
[03:39] Aisha: cool. and what about request logs — do they include token-level timing?
[03:45] Priya: request logs include per-token timing aggregated, and token counts. we also have a separate streaming events view that shows server-sent events and partial outputs.
[03:53] [04:05] Priya: showing the request logs UI — you can query by time range, route, model, customer_id. here's an example query: service:inference AND route:"/generate-chat" AND model.version:"v2027-05-01" | sort by latency desc. we provide saved queries as well.
[04:23] Sam: if we provide our logs, can you run a benchmark and show expected tail latency on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[04:29] Jamie: yes, for POC we run bench harness on your sample logs and show both P99 and P95 on Dedicated profiles and hosted tiers. we'll include batching and prefix cache effects.
[04:38] Lina: about compliance — we need SOC2, iso27001 docs and audit logs for admin actions. are these available?
[04:45] Jamie: yes SOC2 and ISO are available for hosted; for private deployments we can provide a signed attestation and integrate with your audit pipeline. admin action logs are retained per contract — we'll include retention numbers in the security pack.
[04:58] Aisha: what about SSO and RBAC? we use Okta and need role-based access for product vs infra teams.
[05:05] Priya: we support SSO via SAML/Okta and fine-grained RBAC; you can restrict who can view request logs vs who can perform rollouts.
[05:13] [05:25] Priya: jumping back to trace — here's an example where latency is high due to a cache miss and also due to a model kernel fallback. you can expand spans to see GPU microseconds in the kernel span, and also the routing decision span.
[05:40] Marcus: interesting — do you annotate why a fallback happened? e.g., OOM vs model crash?
[05:46] Priya: we annotate the error code and include stderr from the serving runtime when available; for OOMs we show memory usage and stack. sometimes the stack traces are noisy in transcription exports but they are attached in the trace record.
[05:59] Sam: is it possible to export traces to our SIEM or use an alert webhook?
[06:05] Priya: yes, you can configure webhooks for alerts and also export logs/traces to your SIEM via our forwarder.
[06:12] [06:30] Priya: now switching to error analysis view — we surface top error signatures and example failing requests, grouped by fingerprint. you can click a fingerprint to see sample traces and a diff of prompts that led to failure.
[06:45] Aisha: can we pin a set of eval prompts and get notified if regression appears after a rollout?
[06:51] Jamie: yep that's part of Redwood Optimize — you can attach eval sets to a rollout and get quality regression alerts referencing those prompts. we'll demo Optimize later if desired.
[07:03] Marcus: talk to me about private deployment — if we go VPC/on-prem, do we still get the same console?
[07:09] Jamie: yes, the control plane can be customer-managed and the console connects via private networking. audit logs and KMS integration are supported. a few admin features depend on the control plane contract but functionally the console is the same.
[07:21] Lina: in private mode, where does the telemetry live? we can't have telemetry cross the VPC boundary.
[07:27] Priya: you can point telemetry to your internal collector; Redwood can run the observability stack inside your VPC and push only aggregated metrics out if needed. we also support an air-gapped option for very restricted environments.
[07:41] [07:55] Priya: small demo of request logs query — typing a live query: route:"/generate" AND response.contains:"account number" -> returns 12 hits; we offer field redaction so PII can be scrubbed at ingestion.
[08:10] Sam: are there retention controls per field? we want short retention for request bodies but longer for metadata.
[08:16] Priya: yes, retention policy rules can be per-field and per-tenant.
[08:23] [08:35] Priya: now an example debugging flow — a user reported hallucination. search trace, find request, open span timeline, inspect prompt and model.version, note a fallback to compat-small-quant; open nearby requests to see if it was a rollout-related issue. you can annotate the trace and create a bug directly in Jira via our integration.
[08:58] Aisha: ah nice integration. does that include the full request payload automatically?
[09:03] Priya: it's configurable — you can attach anonymized payload or link to the trace id only.
[09:11] [09:25] Marcus: about cost controls — can we route low-sensitivity traffic to smaller models automatically?
[09:31] Jamie: yes, routing policies can be tag-based and you can do rules by route, user, or region. we can also do canary rollouts and automatic fallback if latency spikes.
[09:43] Sam: any gotchas on sampling? we don't want to sample away rare failures.
[09:48] Priya: sampling is configurable; for POC we suggest full capture for a narrow route and tail-sampling for general traffic.
[09:59] [10:12] Priya: quick note — request logs are queryable via SQL-like syntax and also exportable to BigQuery. we also support an API for pulling raw traces.
[10:22] Lina: what about encryption in transit?
[10:25] Jamie: TLS 1.2+/mTLS for private peering, and you can use customer-managed KMS for at-rest keys.
[10:32] [10:45] Priya: demoing a saved filter and an alert — here we set an alert for error-rate > 2% on route /generate-chat for model.version v2027-05-01; when triggered it hits our webhook and creates a ticket. it includes example traces and links.
[10:59] Aisha: good. can we see correlated downstream logs? e.g., our upstream service logs which called Redwood, so we can see end-to-end?
[11:06] Priya: yes, by mapping trace ids you can stitch in upstream logs; if you push upstream trace id in the request headers it joins automatically.
[11:17] Marcus: ok, let's talk POC scope — we want to validate tail latency and regression detection for our main route over 24h of traffic.
[11:24] Jamie: perfect. we'll run a bench with your 24h anonymized logs, show P95/P99 for Dedicated and Hosted, and run Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization.
[11:34] Sam: do you simulate cold KV cache? important for our bursty traffic.
[11:38] Priya: yes, bench harness can replay with cold cache conditions; we'll show both warmed and cold cache baselines.
[11:46] [11:58] Priya: switching back — here's an example of a trace where the kernel selected was an older cuDNN path vs newer fused kernel; it's annotated as kernel_version and you can filter traces by kernel.
[12:10] Marcus: interesting, that'll help debugging perf regressions after infra upgrades.
[12:15] Priya: yep.
[12:18] [12:30] Aisha: what else do we need to succeed in a POC?
[12:34] Jamie: mostly your 24h logs (anonymized), a contact for security review, and a decision on what model variants you want tested. we'll provide the bench results and recommended configs.
[12:45] Lina: I'll check with compliance and share required docs.
[12:49] [13:00] Priya: quick reminder — we have a sample playbook with saved queries and a trace troubleshooting checklist at https://redwood.ai/samples/trace-playbook.
[13:10] Marcus: thanks, can you send that along with pricing?
[13:14] Jamie: yes, I'll send pricing and the Dedicated vs Hosted TCO sheet, plus the security pack.
[13:22] Sam: one last technical — can we run custom instrumentation to surface our own metrics into the trace UI?
[13:29] Priya: you can emit custom spans/attributes via our SDKs. we'd recommend a stable trace_id header so it correlates end-to-end.
[13:38] [13:50] Priya: demo end — recording will be shared. any final Qs?
[13:56] Aisha: none from me, good session.
[14:00] Marcus: we want to do the POC, target week of 6/21.
[14:05] Jamie: great, we'll follow up with calendar invite and next steps.
[14:10] Lina: I'll confirm compliance checklist and get back.
[14:15] Sam: I'll prepare the anonymized logs.
[14:20] Jamie: thanks everyone.

Recap (verbatim-ish):
- Demo covered tracing UI, span timelines, KV cache hit/miss, model variant and fallback annotation, request logs queries, redaction, retention rules, and integrations (Jira, SIEM, BigQuery).
- Customer asks: POC for 24h logs to validate P95/P99 and regression detection; compliance review for SOC2/ISO and KMS; pricing and TCO comparison between Dedicated vs Hosted.
